entities.name: Agostino Cusani
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Agostino Cusani (1615–1686) was an Italian Catholic bishop and cardinal who served in the Roman Curia and as Bishop of Faenza during the mid-seventeenth century. A member of the distinguished Milanese Cusani family that produced several prominent churchmen, he pursued an ecclesiastical career in Rome that brought him to positions of significant administrative responsibility.

As a curial cardinal, Cusani participated in the complex processes of Church governance during a period when the papacy was engaged in delicate political balancing between the major Catholic powers—France, Spain, and the Holy Roman Empire. His role in the Curia placed him in the inner workings of the institution that governed Catholic life across the globe at a time when the Church's institutional apparatus was extensive and politically significant.

The Cusani family's repeated production of bishops and cardinals illustrates the aristocratic nepotism that characterised early modern Catholic governance: noble families from Milan, Rome, and Venice used ecclesiastical offices as instruments of family advancement and political influence. Agostino Cusani's career exemplifies this pattern while also reflecting genuine administrative competence in curial service.
